html:
The Duchy of Modena and Reggio was a small state in the Po valley of northern Italy, ruled by the House of Este, from 1452 to 1859. It is on the map from 1650 to 1815.

The emperor made Borso d'Este duke of Modena and Reggio in 1452. For over a century the Este court sat at Ferrara, a Renaissance centre of poets and painters. When the main line died out in 1597, the pope claimed Ferrara for the Papal States, and the Este moved their capital to Modena in 1598. Their court there kept a great library; the historian Ludovico Antonio Muratori was its librarian.

French armies swept the duke away in 1796, and Modena became part of Napoleon's republics in Italy. In 1814 an Austrian Habsburg heir of the Este came back as duke. Revolts broke out in 1831 and 1848, and in 1859 the duke fled for good. Modena voted to join Piedmont-Sardinia and so Italy.
